articles.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s final: Alexander Zverev v Ben Shelton – live
articles.summary: Men’s final updates from 1pm ET/6pm BST Shelton faces date with destiny | Email Ella. As at every US Open final, the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd will be full of famous faces.
body: Kerrith writes in with a prediction: “Zverev learnt his game playing against his lefty brother Misha (peak rank 25), the very reason why his backend is a brick wall. He’s more prepared for this matchup than people realise I think. Zverev in 3.”

Right to point out that Zverev is better suited than most to handle Shelton’s big serve. It’ll be worth watching how he lines up in the first few games to receive those serves. It does seem Zverev has the edge, but I’d like to see how far Shelton can push him. He’s significantly improved his baseline play and his own backhand from their previous meetings.

When this tournament began, this would have seemed one of the more unlikely combinations to see in the final. In his opener, Ben Shelton lost the first set 1-6 to Tallon Griekspoor. Alexander Zverev was two points from a first-round exit against Lorenzo Sonego. And here we are.

Neither player is a stranger to a marathon match. The incoming Tennis Australia CEO, Andrew Abdo, suggested last month that tennis should rethink the best-of-five format for men’s grand slam matches to attract a younger audience.

articles.title: ‘Just making a joke’: Usain Bolt retracts claim stairs got him out of breath
articles.summary: Jamaican says athletes ‘loving’ Ultimate Championship. Former sprinter proposed to Kasi Bennett last month. A year ago, Usain Bolt revealed he had stopped running and got out of breath whenever he went up the stairs.
body: Bolt, who is an ambassador for the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, laughed as he told reporters that his claims about his lack of fitness in Tokyo last year had been overegged for effect. “I made a joke and you guys took it out of context,” Bolt said, with a grin.
“It was everywhere. I wasn’t running out of breath walking up the stairs. I was just making a joke. I’m in the best shape of my life. Make sure that’s the headline.”

Part of that fitness drive, it appears, is down to his engagement to Bennett, the mother of his three children – Olympia Lightning, Thunder and Saint Leo – who he proposed to on his 40th birthday. “I tell you guys, I’m working out,” Bolt said. “I’ve really been to the gym and working on it every day since I’ve been here. So, I’m trying to get on it and I’m doing well. I’m happy with where I’m at. So let’s continue working on this.”

The 39-year-old Irishman's first career title came in the 2009 tournament when still an amateur, and he now joins 2025 winner Rory McIlroy - whom he won the 2024 Zurich Classic of New Orleans alongside - as a two-time champion.

articles.title: Europe win Solheim Cup against USA to give captain Anna Nordqvist last laugh
articles.summary: Europe beat USA 15-13 after 7-4 win in singles matches. Lottie Woad seals victory with putt against Auston Kim. Eyebrows were raised when Anna Nordqvist somewhat abruptly announced her retirement from competitive golf last month at the age of just 39.
body: What a rousing afternoon this soon became for women’s golf in Europe. The understated Nordqvist was on the podium once more.

The wait for a USA win on foreign soil, stretching back to 2015, goes on. Europe are due huge praise for their singles performance here, which had felt unlikely from a four-session ­position of an 8-8 tie. Nordqvist and her players, including four rookies, were underdogs. On day three, there was seldom any doubt they would upset the odds. The record books will show 15-13 as the margin of victory when, in essence, there was more between the teams on Sunday.

“I think there has just been so many emotions bottled up,” ­Nordqvist said. “It’s just been such a long road. It’s been a lot of hard work. It’s been really hard retiring weeks ago, then doing this and doing them both at the same time.

articles.title: 'Finally got our points' - Hull and Woad shine in European Solheim win
articles.summary: Charley Hull gets the ball rolling as Europe's big guns finally came to the fore in Sunday's singles as they wrestled the Solheim Cup back from the United States with a 15½-12½ victory at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.
body: Charley Hull got the ball rolling as Europe's big names finally came to the fore in Sunday's singles as they wrestled the Solheim Cup back from the USA with a 15-13 victory in the Netherlands.

Hull, who had garnered just half a point across the first two days in an unprofitable partnership with fellow Englishwoman Lottie Woad, led Europe out again on Sunday and claimed a 3&2 win over American livewire Megan Khang.
It delivered an immediate boost to Anna Nordqvist's team in the singles format that they have been unbeaten in since their last home defeat in 2015.

Woad, who alongside Hull is ranked among the top 10 players in the world, also delivered, with her 2&1 win over fellow debutant Auston Kim sparking wild celebrations on the 17th green at Bernardus Golf Club.

articles.title: Houston Texans' honor late co-founder Janice McNair with emotional pregame tribute
articles.summary: The Houston Texans honored their late co-founder Janice McNair with an emotional four-minute ceremony before Sunday's season-opener against the Buffalo Bills at Reliant Stadium. McNair, who died at 89 years old in July, helped found the Texans with her husband Bob McNair, who passed in 2018.
body: "She's just been a wonderful supporter," the late Bob McNair said in a one-minute video that played during the tribute. "She treats people well, cares about people. She likes to raise people up, not knock them down, and always a positive attitude. That's a great asset for me to have."

Janice was known for her philanthropy, starting with The Robert and Janice McNair Foundation that invested millions of dollars into various programs across the city and the Houston Texans Foundation, which raised $50 million in two-plus decades.
"Helping others, that's the biggest thrill," Janice said in the pregame video.

After the video, that included Janice welcoming head coach DeMeco Ryans back to Houston when he was hired as the Texans head coach in 2023, Grammy-award winning soprano Nancy Curtis sang "Amazing Grace" followed by a moment of silence.

articles.title: Haaland proud of personality and character in Manchester derby win
articles.summary: Erling Haaland was full of praise for 10-man City's determination, grit and character to fight and overcome Manchester United 1-0 in the Premier League at Old Trafford. Match Report. Haaland strike wins 199th Manchester derby for resolute 10-man City.
body: Enzo Maresca’s side were dealt a heavy blow after just 23 minutes of the 199th Manchester derby, as Phil Foden was dismissed for violent conduct by referee Michael Oliver.

The Blues had to dig deep and despite the hosts hitting the woodwork twice, we made the breakthough on the hour mark through Haaland, who struck his ninth goal in eight top-flight appearances against the Red Devils.

Enzo Fernández then saw his effort touched onto the post by United goalkeeper Senne Lammens, before City shot-stopper Gianluigi Donnarumma denied Bryan Mbeumo a last-gasp equaliser with a splendid save.

“It hasn’t happened a lot in my lifetime to go down to 10 men so it’s kind of a new experience to win with 10 men. It’s amazing to be honest,” began Haaland in his interview after the game. “We had to lay low, which is not ideal because we like to keep the ball and like to try and score goals. These times you have to go low and take your chances when possible and we managed to do it well.

articles.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
articles.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.
However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

articles.title: 'There's no stopping Antonelli' - Hamilton says 2026 F1 title bid is over
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton appeared to give up hope of claiming a record eighth Formula 1 title this year as he said that "there's no stopping" Kimi Antonelli following the championship leader's latest victory at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Antonelli benefitted from some good fortune at the new all-new Madring circuit to claim his eighth victory of the season, while Hamilton retired early in the race after suffering a brake-pedal issue on his Ferrari.

The victory saw Antonelli extend his lead at the top of the standings over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell to 81 points, while Hamilton fell 101 points back in third, with Norris five points further adrift in fourth.
"I think there's no stopping him and Mercedes this year," Hamilton said of his former team during a post-race interview with Sky Sports F1.

While Antonelli was fortunate on Sunday as the timing of a virtual safety car enabled him to leapfrog McLaren's Lando Norris, who had appeared on course for a comfortable victory, the 20-year-old Italian has driven with supreme consistency in just his second F1 campaign.

articles.summary: Erling Haaland's contentious winner earned 10-man Manchester City a derby win over rivals United at Old Trafford - after Phil Foden's controversial first-half red card.
body: Report and free match highlights as Man City beat Man Utd 1-0 in the Manchester derby; Phil Foden was controversially sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes; United hit the post twice but Erling Haaland put City ahead, but was Enzo Fernandez offside in the build-up for the winner?

City have now joined Arsenal as Premier League title race pace setters with maximum points from four games - but their winning goal against Man Utd was widely branded as not legal. Enzo Fernandez looked to impact play when clearly in an offside position - but the goal was not ruled out.

"When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong," added Neville. "We will see an apology from Pro Ref. There is no doubt that Fernandez is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off."

City will feel justice was done after their job became much harder when Foden was given his marching orders earlier. A tepid first half of the 199th Manchester derby was dominated by Foden's shock sending-off.
